title: Auxiliary Power Unit Intake Flap Sticking in Cold and Contaminated Conditions
abstract: Operator report of auxiliary power unit intake flaps that fail to reach the fully open position at northern outstations in winter, with the resulting starts abandoned and the aircraft dispatched on ground power.

sections.request: At our northern stations we are losing the auxiliary power unit on the first attempt of the day about one morning in five between November and March. The flap indication does not go to open, the start is abandoned, and we end up on a ground cart which we do not always have. Three times last winter we pushed back late because the cart was on another stand. The engineers who have looked at it say the flap is stiff rather than jammed and that once it has been cycled a few times by hand it behaves for the rest of the day. We would like a permanent fix rather than the current advice, which is to cycle the flap during the walk-around. It is minus twenty on that apron and nobody is going to do that reliably.
sections.background: The current bulletin covering the flap actuator was embodied on our twin-engine aircraft in 2019 and 2020 and made the summer behaviour better, but it was never offered for the four-engine aircraft, of which we operate nine on the same routes. Our line maintenance data shows twenty-eight abandoned starts in the last two winters, twenty-one of them on the four-engine fleet. Two operators on the same network report the same pattern.
sections.expected_outcome: An intake flap installation that reaches the fully open position and gives a correct indication at minus thirty degrees with de-icing fluid residue present, available for both the twin-engine and the four-engine fleet, and embodiable at a line check.

type_data.business_justification: Twenty-eight abandoned starts over two winters, each of which either consumes a ground power cart that is not always available or delays a departure; the workaround depends on ramp staff cycling a flap by hand in extreme cold.
